judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the Facebook icon in the AddToAny share row under the article title (name 'Facebook' from an sr-only span). claimTrue: in the capture its href is '/#facebook', which resolves to the home page, so the sentence holds of the captured href. But the live HTML has href='#' and loads addtoany.com/menu/page.js, which writes the '/#facebook' placeholder (with target=_blank and rel=nofollow noopener, as captured) and intercepts the click to open a Facebook share window; the link never takes users to the Home page. captureDiffers: the captured DOM matches what a browser builds for users; the wrong part is the destination record, which followed the script's placeholder href. elementFails: the purpose is sharing this article on Facebook; 'Facebook' in the share list right after the article's h1 lets that be determined, so I judge it passes. A stricter auditor could fail it because the footer has another link named 'Facebook' that goes to ALA's Facebook page, but that would be a share-versus-visit ambiguity, not the Home page mismatch the claim names, so the label is false_positive either way. Cause: the destination given to the model was not where the link leads.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the 'Donate Now' button-styled link in the 'Make a Donation' band. The live CSS sets .btn.secondary-btn to color #0d2354 on background #c4d600, which is 9.36:1, and the full-page screenshot shows exactly those pixels (#c4d600 sampled at the button). The page's own CSS gives the newsletter modal (modaal) an overlay of #0d2354 at opacity 0.8, and the measured colours are exactly the element's colours seen through it: #c4d600 under 80% #0d2354 gives #314743, and the navy text stays #0d2354, so the 1.53:1 is the button seen through the newsletter popup's backdrop. claimTrue: yes for the captured state with that modal open. captureDiffers: yes, the measurement comes from a transient first-visit modal state in which the content behind it is inert; users read this button at full colour once the popup is closed (and on return visits, since it sets a 365-day cookie). elementFails: no, 9.36:1 passes 1.4.3.

But the live page loads the Fundraise Up widget, which intercepts '?form=' links and opens its donation checkout, so the link does what its text says. Even read by text and context alone ('Donate Now' after the heading 'Make a Donation'), the purpose is clear. captureDiffers: the live HTML has the same link and script; nothing differs. elementFails: no. Cause: the destination record (the page refetched without the script) is not where the link leads.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer newsletter field (input type=text, name=cons_email, aria-label and placeholder 'Email Address') under 'Become a Lung Health Insider', which collects the visitor's own email address. claimTrue: it has autocomplete='off', which does not identify the purpose. elementFails: email is one of the WCAG 2.1 input purposes, and with autocomplete='off' and no 'email' token (technique H98 not used) the purpose cannot be programmatically determined, so the field fails 1.3.5. captureDiffers: the live HTML has the same input with autocomplete='off'. The claim names that failure.
